label: Trigger
description: Entry point that starts a workflow. Supports manual runs, form submissions (Gravity Forms, WPForms, Contact Form 7, Ninja Forms, Elementor), inbound webhooks, WordPress core events, another workflow's output, and RSS feeds.

config.name: content
config.description: Text payload for a manual trigger.

config.name: selectedForm
config.description: Form id reference for form triggers.

config.name: selectedFields
config.description: Form field objects captured from the submission.

config.name: webhookUrl
config.description: Generated unique inbound URL for a webhook trigger.

config.name: webhookKeys
config.description: Key mapping objects for the webhook payload.

config.name: selectedWpCoreTrigger
config.description: WordPress core event to listen for.

config.name: wpCoreTriggerConditions
config.description: Trigger-specific conditions for the WordPress core event.

config.name: selectedWorkflow
config.description: Source workflow id when triggerType is workflowOutput.

config.name: rssSettings
config.description: RSS feed url, polling interval, maxItems, filters.

example.content: Draft a welcome email for a new customer.

produces.reference: [Input from {id}] for the whole payload; [[Field Label] from {id}] for a specific form/webhook field
produces.note: A manual trigger produces one text blob ([Input from {id}]). Form/webhook/RSS triggers expose named fields whose names are the submitted field labels/keys; these are known only at runtime, so [[label] from {id}] references are ALLOWED and are NOT hard-failed by the validator.
